Esos modelos suman 942.980 descargas de 2.065.693 en el Top 30 (45,6 %). Abajo está el código para reproducir la cifra con la API pública.

El campo downloads que devuelve la API de modelos es una ventana móvil de 30 días. Premia lo que se está usando ahora, no lo que lleva años publicado. Por eso un modelo lanzado hace seis semanas puede superar a uno de 2024.

Para este recuento usamos el ranking de descargas de modelos de lenguaje (text-generation e image-text-to-text), con una lista explícita de cuentas oficiales de desarrolladores coreanos (LG AI Research, SK Telecom, Upstage, KRAFTON, NAVER, Kakao, KT, VIDRAFT y otras). Un modelo cuenta solo si lo publica directamente la cuenta oficial del desarrollador.

El primer puesto es POCKET-Darwin-180B-GGUF, publicado el 2 de octubre de 2026: en menos de dos meses acumula 715.709 descargas totales, de las cuales 491.707 caen en los últimos 30 días. POCKET-35B-GGUF, publicado el 22 de julio, acumula 2.084.270 descargas totales y 307.524 en la ventana actual.

Sumando todos los modelos de cada empresa en la ventana de 30 días, VIDRAFT (cuentas FINAL-Bench y VIDraft) llega a 964.680 descargas. Le siguen SK Telecom (88.901), KRAFTON (74.906), LG AI Research (53.129), Kakao (17.450) y Upstage (6.405). Dentro del Top 30 coreano, los tres modelos POCKET reúnen 942.980 de 2.065.693 descargas, es decir, el 45,6 %.

En el panorama global (Top 300 por descargas a 30 días) el reparto por país de origen es 71,2 % China y 26,5 % Estados Unidos. Un ranking propio por desarrollador permite ver qué modelos coreanos descarga de verdad la comunidad.

Los tres modelos del podio son versiones GGUF pensadas para ejecutarse localmente con llama.cpp y herramientas compatibles, sin GPU de centro de datos. Cuando el coste de entrada baja de "alquilar un clúster" a "descargar un archivo", el número de personas que prueban el modelo crece, y las descargas lo reflejan.

Con unas pocas líneas de Python se consultan los modelos más descargados de una organización:

Los números cambian cada día porque la ventana es móvil; las cifras de este artículo corresponden a la captura del 21 de noviembre de 2026. Para ver el ranking completo con filtros por país, tamaño y cuantización existe el tablero público Global LLM Download Leaderboard, que se actualiza a diario.

¿Qué modelo coreano de lenguaje es el más descargado? En la ventana de 30 días al 21 de noviembre de 2026, POCKET-Darwin-180B-GGUF de VIDRAFT, con 491.707 descargas.

¿Qué significa que downloads sea una ventana de 30 días? Que la API cuenta las descargas de los últimos 30 días, no el total histórico. Refleja el uso reciente.

#9790. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9787. Same Character, 25 Clips: How ULTRA Was Made

Posted on Nov 21 • Originally published at characterlock.wordpress.com

Originally published on the Character Lock blog.

ULTRA is a 3-minute AI brand film (3:13) with one bear dad holding across more than 25 clips. It was made with a method called Character Lock: define the character once, lock it on a sheet, direct every shot against that sheet, and check every frame before delivery. Here is how it was actually made, step by step.

ULTRA sent a script and a reference ad: a dad always on edge, and a friend who quietly switched to a zero-nicotine pouch. The film had to carry that story for three minutes, in a kitchen, a garage and a truck, with the product readable in every shot.

A three-minute story lives or dies on its characters. In AI video they drift: a face changes, a shirt changes colour, a label melts, and across more than 25 clips that adds up to a different person by the end. One good clip proves nothing; twenty-five matching clips prove the system.

Make the dad a grizzly and his best friend a golden Labrador. Animals stop the scroll and carry the emotion without a casting call, as long as each stays the same animal in every scene. The viewer feels seen as a stressed dad: the bear carries the same tension. The switch is shown without a word: the old silver tin in the kitchen bin.

Dad on edge in the kitchen, morning. The garage: his friend notices the tension. The confession: "Ten months ago I switched to this." The product hero: the tin on the bench in a patch of sun. Dad's turn: "Why doesn't anyone talk about this?" The switch: the new pouch, the old tin in the bin. The end line: "Same ritual. Zero nicotine. No crash."

Ehsaan is the same system run in the other direction: one actor plays six roles in a single film, each held apart from the others. Holding one character steady across 25 clips and holding six apart in one film are the same skill: a lock, a sheet and a frame-by-frame check.

No method can promise a character will be identical in every frame. The models do not allow it, and the tools admit it themselves. What the method promises is the system: a turnaround sheet, identity marks, and a frame-by-frame check on every clip. ULTRA is the proof that the system holds across a full film. The same system, in worksheet form, is the free Character Lock Kit.

#9785. Benchmarking AWS Amplify, Lambda, Web Functions, and ECS for Next.js

"Should this run on Amplify, Lambda or ECS?" is usually answered with a feature list. I wanted numbers. So I took one Next.js app, deployed it to four AWS runtimes in the same account and Region, including the new Lambda Web Functions, and measured the things that decide the choice in practice: latency under load, cold starts, CPU speed, real limits, and the monthly bill at four traffic levels.

Lambda and ECS run the exact same container image, and the Web Function runs the same files from a .zip. Amplify Hosting builds the same Git commit. Every command, script, and result is in a public repository, with deploy and cleanup steps:

One app, four runtimes, one DynamoDB table:

The app has a few endpoints, each testing something different:

Every response reports which runtime served it, the CPU architecture, and whether it was the first request of that process (a cold start):

Everything runs in eu-central-1. Lambda and Fargate use arm64 (Graviton) and roughly the same size: Lambda with 1024 MB of memory, and a Fargate task with 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB. A Web Function environment has a fixed size of 2 arm64 vCPUs and 2 GB, which you can't change, and Amplify chooses its own compute.

While the setup is running, the only fixed cost is the ECS part: the load balancer, one Fargate task and four public IPv4 addresses, about $1.90 per day. Lambda, Amplify and DynamoDB cost close to nothing at test traffic. Run the cleanup script when you are done.

The app is a normal Next.js app router project. The only special setting is the standalone output, which produces a small self-contained server.js for the container. Amplify builds the app its own way, so the setting is applied only in the Docker build:

The Dockerfile is where Lambda and ECS meet:

--provenance=false keeps a plain single-platform image. By default, buildx adds an attestation manifest and pushes an image index, which Lambda may refuse to use. The script tags each image with the Git commit, so an immutable tag always matches one commit.

Scan on push found one critical CVE on the first push, in zlib from the node:22-alpine base image, not in the app. Base images are rebuilt on a schedule, so security fixes can be days old before they reach the tag you pull. One line in the final stage fixed it:

The next image scanned with zero findings. The compressed image is 88 MB in ECR (233 MB unpacked).

The DynamoDB table is on-demand with one item. Each runtime gets its own IAM role with exactly one permission, dynamodb:GetItem on this table.

A public Function URL now needs both permissions: lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl, and lambda:InvokeFunction limited to calls that come through the URL. I removed the second one to check, and the URL answered with 403 and a helpful message:

A Function URL is free and needs no API Gateway. For production, you would usually put CloudFront in front of it for a custom domain, caching and AWS WAF.

The documented default is 1,000 concurrent executions, but my account had 10. Ten concurrent requests at about 100 ms each is roughly 100 requests per second, and anything above returns 429 Too Many Requests. I requested an increase in Service Quotas (quota code L-B99A9384).

The increase to 1,000 was approved automatically after 2 hours and 20 minutes. Lambda's fast endpoints need far less concurrency than you might expect: at about 40 ms per request, 50 requests per second keep only 2 to 3 environments busy. The CPU endpoint at 50 requests per second peaked at 57 concurrent executions, well over the original limit.

Lambda Web Functions are a new kind of Lambda function for HTTP traffic. Your code is a normal web server that listens on a port, Lambda gives it an HTTPS endpoint, and each execution environment serves many requests at the same time, like a container. It still scales to zero when there is no traffic.

The Next.js standalone server reads HOSTNAME and PORT instead, so the entry file maps one to the other:

To keep the comparison fair, I didn't rebuild the app. The deploy script copies /app out of the same linux/arm64 container image, adds index.js, and deploys that folder:

--include-hidden-files is easy to miss: the Next.js build lives in .next, and without the flag the command leaves hidden folders out of the package. deploy creates the S3 bucket, the function, the first revision and a public endpoint, and waits until the endpoint is active. My first deploy took under a minute.

A revision is an immutable snapshot of code and configuration. Changing an environment variable means a new revision, and an endpoint can route traffic to one revision or split it between two, which gives you canary deployments without CodeDeploy.

The pricing model is different from classic Lambda. In eu-central-1 you pay $0.30 per million requests, $0.000035 per vCPU-second of CPU time that your code actually uses, and $0.0000046 per GB-second of memory for the whole life of each environment. A request that waits for DynamoDB uses almost no CPU, so it costs very little. But an environment that stays alive costs memory time even between requests: one environment kept alive for a month is about $24 in memory alone.

A Fargate task in a private subnet needs a NAT gateway or VPC endpoints to pull its image, and either costs more than the task itself. For this test, the tasks run in public subnets with a public IP, and the security groups do the protecting:

Two roles, two jobs: the execution role lets ECS pull the image and write logs, and the task role is what your code runs as. The DynamoDB permission goes on the task role only.

Two settings save time on every deploy. The target group health check uses /api/health every 10 seconds with a healthy threshold of 2, so a new task gets traffic in about 20 seconds. The deregistration delay is 10 seconds instead of the default 300, so an old task stops quickly.

One bug from my script is worth sharing: --output text separates a list of subnet IDs with tabs, not spaces. My script turned spaces into commas, so the service request got one "subnet ID" with tabs inside and failed with Subnet ID must match subnet-[0-9a-f]+. Pipe the list through tr '\t' ' '.

Amplify Hosting connects to GitHub with its own GitHub App. It does not use an AWS CodeConnections connection, even if you already have one for CodeBuild or CodePipeline. So the first step is in the console: Create new app, GitHub, choose the repository and the main branch. Amplify detects Next.js and uses the amplify.yml from the repository.

This is the biggest surprise for anyone coming from Lambda or ECS. Amplify passes environment variables to the build, not to the server-side code at runtime. The fix is to write the variables your server code needs into .env.production during the build:

The || true is there because my first build failed without it. Before the variables were set, grep found nothing and exited with code 1, and Amplify stopped the build with "Command failed with exit code 1".

Two more rules: variable names can't start with AWS_, so the app reads APP_REGION instead of AWS_REGION, and secrets should not go into .env.production this way, because they end up in the build artifact.

The server-side code needs AWS credentials to call DynamoDB. Amplify calls this a compute role: an IAM role that amplify.amazonaws.com can assume.

Without a compute role, the page renders but the DynamoDB call fails with a credentials error.

The first response from Amplify answered a question the console doesn't:

AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_MEMORY_SIZE is set, so the server code runs on Lambda with 1024 MB, on x64, managed by Amplify. You can't choose the memory size or arm64, and it doesn't count against your account's Lambda concurrency quota.

At 10 requests per second (p50 / p95 / p99 in milliseconds, 1,200 requests each):

On light requests, ECS is the fastest, Lambda and the Web Function are close behind with almost the same medians, and Amplify is about 1.5 times slower than Lambda. ECS wins here because nothing sits between the load balancer and a warm Node.js process.

The CPU row is the surprise. One Fargate task with 0.5 vCPU could not keep up with 10 CPU-heavy requests per second: each request needs about 80 to 150 ms of CPU, so the work arrived faster than half a vCPU could do it. Requests queued, the ALB health checks timed out, and ECS replaced the "unhealthy" task in the middle of the test. 8% of requests failed and the median rose to 1.9 seconds. Lambda, the Web Function and Amplify handled the same load without errors, because they add execution environments as the load grows.

The lesson is not that ECS is slow. A fixed-size service needs auto scaling and headroom, and a health check that shares the CPU with the work it checks can turn an overload into a restart.

At 200 requests per second (p50 / p95 / p99 in milliseconds, 24,000 requests each):

Lambda, the Web Function and Amplify barely noticed the twentyfold increase: their medians moved by a few milliseconds and no request failed. For the Web Function, I ran the 200 requests per second test twice, because AWS says the first load test on a new Web Function scales conservatively, and the table shows the second run. The two runs were within a few milliseconds of each other. Lambda scaled to 234 concurrent executions in the first seconds of the test, then settled between 50 and 90, with zero throttles.

The single ECS task reached 100% CPU and failed. At 50 requests per second the same task used about 65% CPU on the page endpoint, so one 0.5 vCPU task handles roughly 70 page requests per second before it falls over. For real traffic, you would run at least two tasks with target tracking auto scaling at 50 to 60% CPU.

The 50 requests per second results look like the 10 requests per second ones for Lambda, ECS and Amplify, so I left them in the repository instead of adding another table.

One more number explains why Lambda looks so fast: its billed duration (the CloudWatch Duration metric) was 9 to 16 ms at the median for the light endpoints. Most of the 40 ms that the client sees is the network and the Function URL, not your code.

The CPU endpoint does the same 50,000 hashes everywhere:

Lambda gives CPU in proportion to memory: one full vCPU at 1,769 MB. At 1024 MB you get a bit more than half a vCPU, and you pay for the milliseconds you use. A Web Function environment always has 2 vCPUs, and you pay only for the CPU time you use. Node.js runs JavaScript on one thread, so a single request can use only one of them, but that one is a full vCPU. Fargate gives you exactly the vCPU you reserve, all the time, whether you use it or not.

Lambda, 10 forced cold starts (the script changes an environment variable before each request):

Amplify, one request after 20 minutes without traffic, 3 times: 1.94 s, 2.00 s and 0.33 s, compared with about 0.16 s for a warm request. All three were served by a new process, so the third one probably landed on an environment that Amplify had already prepared. You can't see or control this, so plan for about 2 seconds on the first request after a quiet period.

Web Function, 5 forced cold starts (each run creates a new revision, which starts new environments):

ECS has no cold start while a task is running, which is what you pay the fixed monthly price for. Scaling out is a different story: in the ECS events, a replacement task registered with the load balancer about 25 seconds after it started, and then needed two 10-second health checks before it got traffic. A new Lambda environment was ready in about one second.

I asked each runtime to wait longer and longer, and to return larger and larger responses:

If your app has report downloads, file exports or slow third-party calls, these limits decide more than any latency number. Classic Lambda can go beyond 6 MB with response streaming, but that needs code changes. With Web Functions, you get it without changes.

Prices are on-demand prices in eu-central-1 from the AWS Price List API, in November 2026, without free tiers:

Web Functions publish their own usage in CloudWatch (EnvironmentCPUTime, EnvironmentActiveTime and ExecutedRequests in the AWS/Lambda/Web namespace), so I could calculate the real bill for my load tests instead of estimating it:

71% of the bill was memory. At 200 requests per second, Lambda ran up to 55 environments, and none of them served more than 2 requests at the same time (the EnvironmentConcurrentRequests maximum). That was the case in both 200 requests per second runs. AWS documents that a new Web Function starts with a conservative per-environment concurrency limit and raises it as it learns, but I didn't see that happen in about 25 minutes of testing. About 30% of the memory time came after the test, while the environments waited about 5 minutes before Lambda removed them.

The same request mix on classic Lambda would cost about $0.15, or $1.04 per million requests. So in my test, Web Functions cost about four times as much. If the per-environment concurrency grows over time, as AWS describes, this gap will shrink, so treat it as the cost of a new function under a load test, not a final verdict.

For the monthly bill, I used the measured durations: 20 ms of Lambda billed time per request (the 9 to 16 ms median, rounded up), and 5 KB per response. Amplify doesn't publish its billed compute time per request; its CloudWatch Latency metric averaged about 100 ms, which includes the CDN, so I show 100 ms as the upper bound and 30 ms as a likely lower bound. ECS uses the measured capacity of about 50 requests per second per task with headroom. For the Web Function, I used 27 ms of CPU per request, at least one environment alive all month (requests arrive more often than every 5 minutes at these levels), and the measured 0.24 environments per request per second at steady load.

The script is in the repository (bench/cost.py), so you can run it with your own durations and response sizes.

The same build runs on classic Lambda, Web Functions and ECS, so this is not a one-way decision. The Web Function in this article is the same /app folder as the container image, plus a 5-line index.js. Starting on Lambda and moving when your traffic or your limits change is a reasonable path.

The script deletes the Amplify app, the ECS service, cluster, load balancer and target group, the Lambda function, the Web Function and its code versions in the shared awscli-lambdaweb-* bucket, the security groups, the ECR repository, the DynamoDB table, the log groups and the IAM roles. Everything it created has the tag project=runtime-benchmark, so you can check in Tag Editor that nothing is left.

The feature lists told me that ECS is "more powerful", Lambda is "serverless" and Amplify is "easy". The measurements told a more useful story. The always-on container was the fastest per request and the first to fail, because one task is a fixed amount of CPU. The three serverless options were a little slower per request but did not care whether traffic was 10 or 200 requests per second. The newest one, Lambda Web Functions, removes most of classic Lambda's limits and was the fastest on CPU, but its memory billing made it the most expensive serverless option in my test. And the limits that matter most for real apps, request timeout and response size, differ by an order of magnitude between them.

If you only take one thing from this article: measure your own app on the runtime you plan to use, before you choose. The repository makes that a few commands, and the cleanup script removes everything when you are done.

#9784. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9783. How I Automated 10M+ Network KPI Records a Day with Python and Apache Airflow

Posted on Nov 21 • Originally published at pmpdilshan.github.io

Originally published on pmpdilshan.github.io.

Every hour, a mobile network generates performance counters for every cell: traffic, drops, handovers, throughput, congestion. At Mobitel that adds up to more than 10 million KPI records a day. For a long time, turning that into reports meant exporting files, merging them in Excel and rebuilding the same charts every morning.

So I built pipelines in Python and Apache Airflow to do it automatically. They cut manual reporting effort by about 40%. Here's the pattern, and what I'd tell anyone building something similar.

Airflow ties it together. Each step is a task, the dependencies are explicit, and if something fails you can see exactly where and rerun just that part.

The most dangerous pipeline isn't the one that fails. It's the one that succeeds with bad data. A late file, a missing region or a changed column name can silently produce a report that looks fine and is wrong. Checking inputs before processing them saved me more than once.

Things will fail: a server is down, a file is late. If rerunning a task creates duplicates or overwrites good data, every failure becomes a manual clean-up. Designing each step so it can run twice with the same result (idempotency) makes recovery a click instead of an afternoon.

When three reports each calculate "drop rate" slightly differently, meetings turn into arguments about whose number is right. Defining each KPI once, in the pipeline, means everyone works from the same truth.

I didn't start with machine learning. I started with the report everyone hated building. Once the data was flowing reliably, more interesting work like ML-based anomaly detection became possible, because the foundation was there.

Because one day you will. Clear logs saying what ran, how many rows and what was skipped turn a mystery into a five-minute fix.

About 40% less time spent on manual reporting, consistent numbers across teams, and more time for actual optimization work. The lesson I'd pass on: stop building reports. Build the thing that builds reports.

Pathum Dilshan is an RF & Network Planning Engineer at Mobitel, Sri Lanka, and an MSc Data Science & AI student at the University of Moratuwa. He writes about telecom, data and AI. Connect on LinkedIn or visit pmpdilshan.github.io.

#9779. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

  

 The marketing industry is turning to artificial intelligence (AI) as a way to save time and execute smarter, more personalized campaigns. 61% of marketers say AI software is the most important aspect of their data strategy.

  If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

1. Jasper Ai(Formerly known as Jarvis)


Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.

Key Features

  •  It's trusted by 50,000+ marketers for creating engaging marketing campaigns, ad copy, blog posts, and articles within minutes which would traditionally take hours or days. Special Features:
  • Blog posts have been optimized for search engines and rank high on Google and other search engines. This is a huge plus for online businesses that want to generate traffic to their website through content marketing.
  • 99.9% Original Content and guarantees that all content it generates will be original, so businesses can focus on their online reputation rather than worrying about penalties from Google for duplicate content.
  • Long-Form Article Writing – Jasper.ai is also useful for long-form writing, allowing users to create articles of up to 10,000 words without any difficulty. This is ideal for businesses that want to produce in-depth content that will capture their audience’s attention.

The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

3. Seventh Sense

  Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers

  • Creates tailored language models for every customer

  Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. 8. MarketMuse 

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Key features:

  • The built-in editor shows how in-depth your topic is covered and what needs improvement
  • Finds gaps and opportunities for new content creation, prioritized by their probable impact and your chance of ranking

9. Copilot

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Key features:

  • Analyzes customer feedback and sentiments to help you improve your products

11. Albert AI

  Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

  Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

Key features:

  • Breaks down large amounts of data to help you customize campaigns
  • Plugs into your marketing technology stack and can be used across diverse media outlets, including email, content, paid media, and mobile

Final Saying

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. #9777. How long can butter sit out?: For the best baking success, here's the deal on saving softened butter for later.

The bakers of King Arthur are here to solve the kitchen conundrums you share with us, whether it’s on the phone, computer, or by the good old postal service. In Ask the Baker’s Hotline, Annabelle will pick the brains of the talented King Arthur Baker’s Hotline team to tackle some of your most-asked questions.

Ryan from our Baker’s Hotline is here with the answer.

You sure can! It will still work the next time you want to bake. But remember, as with any dairy product, there are always precautions to take.

The USDA recommends keeping butter at room temperature for no more than two days to prevent spoilage. Salt is a preservative and can lengthen the shelf life, but for the sake of this article, we’re talking about unsalted butter. (It’s more appropriate for baking and is the type called for in most King Arthur recipes.)

“If the butter has only been on the counter at room temperature for a few hours or overnight and has maintained a temperature below 70°F, it should be just fine to place back in the fridge,” says Ryan. “You may not notice a difference in the performance of the butter when you eventually use it, other than the wrapper being a bit wet or soft. Food safety-wise, it’s still good to use.”

“If the butter became very soft or started to melt during its time on the counter (or in the microwave if you were speeding up the process), you can put it back in the fridge, but it may not be the best to use in your recipe,” Ryan suggests. “You may notice when it solidifies that it’s separated or grainy. The water, fats, and solids in butter are an emulsion, which can break when melted and re-solidified.” If your recipe depends on butter to create air or structure, like a cake that calls for creaming butter and sugar, you’ll want to start over with new butter.

“If you used that butter in a recipe requiring creaming, the air you incorporate wouldn’t be as stable since the structure of the butter has changed,” Ryan says. “Your baked goods may not rise properly, and frostings may be soft and loose. Is it still safe to use? Food safety-wise, yes. But structure-wise, perhaps not.”

That butter can still be used for other things though! Extra-softened or even melted and re-solidified butter will still work perfectly to spread on toast or pancakes, to be made into brown butter, or to remelt and use in recipes calling for melted butter like a Graham Cracker Crust.

If your butter has been unrefrigerated for more than two days, you run the risk of it going rancid. As Ryan says, “There is no coming back from rancid butter.” It has a distinctly unpleasant flavor and a noticeable rancid smell that carries over into baked goods. It’s best to dispose of the butter if this happens.

But what if you want to keep your butter at room temperature for days at a time to slather on your morning toast? Ryan recommends storing your butter in a butter keeper if you want to leave it on the counter. “The water in the base of the jar creates an airtight seal, helping prevent the butter from spoiling. So long as it is stored away from direct heat and light, the butter in a container like this will be fine for a few days. Be sure to replace the water often and clean the container before filling again.”

“When working with butter in a recipe, I like to bring out and soften only the amount that is needed for what I am working on. That way, I don’t end up with extra butter that won’t be used right away,” he says. “Repeatedly moving butter from the fridge to the counter and then back invites spoilage and poor performance.”

In a rush? To soften your butter more quickly, Ryan advises, “Cut your butter into pats and place them on a plate in a single layer at room temperature. More surface area means that the butter will soften a bit faster!”

#9774. What is piloncillo? This sweetener makes great cookies, pan dulce, and more: Use this traditional Mexican unrefined sugar for a dash of flavor and history.

This article is part of our feature celebrating Pan Dulce. Find all things pan dulce here.

Categorically, piloncillo is a “non-centrifugal” cane sugar, meaning it is an unrefined sugar product and a true natural brown sugar. It’s mostly consumed in Mexico and Latin America, but a similar product can be found in Asia, known as jaggery in India. Though often lumped together, these unrefined dark sugars are very different from brown sugars on the market today, which have been refined to a large degree — in some cases, they’re actually just white sugar with coloring or molasses added.

Making piloncillo, on the other hand, involves an artisanal process that’s hundreds of years old. To make it, pressed cane juice is boiled to evaporate the water and deeply caramelize the sugar. The cooked cane is then poured into molds (often made of wood) and left to dry and harden. Traditional piloncillo is conical in shape and can vary in size from small to large cones but is most commonly found in a medium size that weighs about 200 grams. In Guatemala and Colombia, it is called panela, where it is cooked to a lighter degree and typically formed into a brick, rather than cone, shape. Other forms of piloncillo can be granulated or liquid (which is more rare).

Minimally processed and boldly flavored, piloncillo was historically a prized and respected foodstuff. As an unrefined cane sugar, piloncillo provides more complex vitamins and minerals than refined sugars, which undergo processing and whitening methods that also strip nutrients from the whole food. And piloncillo is also great for baking, providing notes of burnt caramel and hints of smoke. Plus, its rich molasses qualities keep baked goods moist and fresh for longer.

Always look at the ingredient label when purchasing piloncillo and make sure it says 100% pure cane juice or cane sugar. It is becoming increasingly common to find imitation products marketed as jaggery or piloncillo that contain coloring and corn syrup. You can find good piloncillo at specialty grocery stores or online at retailers.

In Mexico and throughout Latin America, piloncillo is an important ingredient in many traditional dishes. (Some will even say it’s not the “real dish” if you substitute sugar in these recipes due to the deep flavors and richness that only piloncillo can provide.) This deep, dark unrefined sugar lends its characteristic flavor and texture to popular foods and beverages such as capirotada, tepache, coyotas, atole, café de olla, calabaza al horno, coricos, and hojarascas, to name a few!

I love adding piloncillo when I’m making champurrado. In this warm and thick chocolate beverage, the piloncillo is chopped or grated and dissolved in the pot with water or milk before adding the chocolate and masa. In this recipe, the piloncillo’s intense sweet and smoky flavors pair well with the chocolate and corn masa.

While there are many dishes and uses for piloncillo, it’s not a simple substitution for granulated white sugar in recipes, but you can use it the same as you would brown sugar with a 1:1 substitution by weight.  Depending on how hard the cone is, it can be crumbled or grated for easier measuring. If it is very hard, try cutting it in half with a sharp knife and then placing it between parchment paper or a towel and beating with a rolling pin.

#9772. Speaking Faster Can Make You More Persuasive — Until This Happens

Your best argument may lose its edge if listeners struggle to keep up with how quickly you deliver it.

Your best argument may lose its edge if listeners struggle to keep up with how quickly you deliver it.

Speaking at a lively pace can make a strong argument more convincing, but rushing can weaken its impact.

Very fast speech makes it harder for listeners to weigh up what they hear, reducing the advantage that good reasons have over weak ones.

The findings suggest that persuading someone depends partly on giving them enough opportunity to think.

The conclusions come from six experiments involving almost 4,000 people who listened to persuasive messages delivered at different speeds.

Across the experiments, increasing the pace from very slow speech initially improved impressions of the speaker’s confidence and encouraged closer consideration of the message.

However, these benefits eventually weakened or reversed as the delivery became faster.

This helps explain why simply telling someone to speak more quickly is incomplete advice.

A faster delivery can make an argument easier to engage with until the listener begins struggling to keep up.

Crucially, the consequences depend on whether the reasons being offered stand up to scrutiny.

In the two main experiments, listeners heard a proposal that would allow university students to pay lower tuition fees in exchange for working part-time.

Some heard strong arguments emphasising benefits such as smaller classes and better services.

Others heard weak arguments that included reduced leisure time and superficial improvements to the campus.

The recordings were digitally altered to change speaking speed while keeping other vocal features, such as pitch and intonation, unchanged.

Participants then rated their support for the proposal, with some also recording the thoughts that had occurred to them while listening.

The combined results showed that strong arguments gained an increasing advantage over weak ones as speech became faster, but lost some of that advantage at higher speeds.

In other words, delivery affected how effectively listeners distinguished a convincing case from an unconvincing one.

A central part of persuasion is how carefully people consider the reasons they are given.

When listeners examine a message closely, they have more opportunity to recognise its strengths, spot its weaknesses and form their own reactions.

This benefits a strong argument, while exposing the shortcomings of a weak one.

Very fast delivery can interfere with that process, making the merits of the message less influential.

The analyses suggested that changes in how easily listeners felt they could follow the reasoning helped explain this pattern.

Although speaking speed also affected how confident the speaker sounded, confidence alone did not adequately explain the overall pattern.

One possible reason very slow speech is less effective is that it makes sustaining attention more demanding, while excessively fast speech leaves too little time to absorb the content.

The experiments tested seven speaking speeds, ranging from 113 to 218 words per minute, but did not establish one ideal pace.

The most effective delivery is likely to depend on factors including the complexity of the message, the audience and the presence of distractions.

The findings also concern recorded persuasive messages, so they do not establish a universal rule for every conversation or public speech.

For someone presenting a strong case, the findings suggest keeping the delivery lively while giving listeners time to follow the reasoning.

Rushing may reduce the very scrutiny that would otherwise make a good argument convincing.

The study was published in the Journal of Nonverbal Behavior (Guyer et al., 2025).

Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean

#9764. For Creamier, Crispier Grilled Cheese, Make It Disneyland-Style

Is there anything more magical than a visit to Disneyland in sunny, beautiful Anaheim, California? While the kids might associate this theme park with their favorite Disney characters or the delightful rides and themed areas, many adults make the pricey trek with an additional consideration in mind: the food. In the theme park where Doritos were first served, one can't-miss creation is the Grilled Cheese Sandwich found at the Jolly Holiday Bakery Cafe (as well as Woody's Lunch Box at Walt Disney World in Florida). If you wanted to replicate its creamy, crispy goodness at home, you might already have the ingredients in your fridge: You'll just need cream cheese for the inside and mayonnaise for the outside.

Disney actually released the recipe during COVID for its grilled cheese sandwich, which features three different cheeses, as well as a garlic mayo spread for the outside. There's cheddar and provolone, but the cream cheese is the star, as it gets oh-so-gooey and decadent when it melts down, and it adds a slight tang that will make your tongue take immediate interest.

You might use butter when making your grilled cheeses, but trust us, switching to mayo is the move because it is scientifically disposed to create a more even, crisper crust. Think about it: You can spread it easily in an even layer without worrying about tearing the bread, as you might with butter. And the inclusion of garlic is a master stroke that introduces even more flavorful depth to what is, essentially, a simple sandwich.

Using cream cheese as a filling and mayonnaise as an outer agent of browning is just one way to achieve the grilled cheese of your dreams. While you should absolutely try these two ingredients, we have a few other ideas that can help you achieve the upgraded Disney Parks-inspired sandwich. The first? Cream cheese is just one of three cheeses that go into this toastie; you'll likely use sliced provolone, but at least for the cheddar, you should grate your own. Blocks of cheese that are grated simply melt better than the pre-shredded variety because there are additional ingredients in the latter that help to keep it from clumping, which prohibits it from melting as wonderfully. If you're going to the trouble of including cream cheese to up the gooey-factor, you might as well go full-tilt where the cheddar is concerned. Disney also includes a bit of cream in its cream cheese blend, which will undeniably enhance the richness of the sandwich and keep things gooey for longer. One tablespoon per quarter cup of cream cheese is more than enough.

To ensure that the sandwich gets its crispiest crust, too, it's important that you don't drop it into the skillet until the pan is fully heated through(though you can still sprinkle salt onto the pan if you want a little extra seasoning). This is so that the golden outsides can start crisping immediately. At the same time, though, you don't want to have the heat turned up too high — a nice medium to medium-low will do the trick. Any hotter and the outside will burn before the cheese has an opportunity to melt all the way through — not the kind of crispness we're seeking.

#9761. Top 10 AI Tools in 2023 That Will Make Your Life Easier



 In this article, we explore the top 10 AI tools that are driving innovation and efficiency in various industries. These tools are designed to automate repetitive tasks, improve workflow, and increase productivity. The tools included in our list are some of the most advanced and widely used in the market, and are suitable for a variety of applications. Some of the tools focus on natural language processing, such as ChatGPT and Grammarly, while others focus on image and video generation, such as DALL-E and Lumen5. Other tools such as OpenAI Codex, Tabnine, Canva, Jasper AI,, and Surfer SEO are designed to help with specific tasks such as code understanding content writing and website optimization. This list is a great starting point for anyone looking to explore the possibilities of AI and how it can be applied to their business or project.

So let’s dive into

1. ChatGPT

ChatGPT is a large language model that generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts. It can be used for tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion. It can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing, and generates coherent and fluent text, but should be used with care as it may generate text that is biased, offensive, or factually incorrect.

Pros:

  • Generates human-like responses to a variety of prompts
  • Can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as language translation, question answering, and text completion
  • Can handle a wide range of topics and styles of writing
  • Can generate coherent and fluent text, even when completing a given text prompt.

Cons:

  • May generate text that is biased or offensive
  • Can generate text that is not accurate or factually correct
  • May require large amounts of computational resources to run
  • The model can sometimes generate text that is not coherent or fluent, depending on the prompt given.

Overall, ChatGPT is a powerful tool for natural language processing, but it should be used with care and with an understanding of its limitations.

2. DALL-E

DALL-E is a generative model developed by OpenAI that is capable of generating images from text prompts. It is based on the GPT-3 architecture, which is a transformer-based neural network language model that has been trained on a massive dataset of text. DALL-E can generate images that are similar to a training dataset and it can generate high-resolution images that are suitable for commercial use.

Pros:

  • Generates high-resolution images
  • Can generate images from text prompts
  • It can be fine-tuned for specific tasks such as generating images of a certain style or category

Cons:

  • May generate images that are not entirely original and could be influenced by the training data
  • May require significant computational resources to run
  • The quality of the generated images may vary depending on the specific prompt

Overall, DALL-E is a powerful AI-based tool for generating images, it can be used for a variety of applications such as creating images for commercial use, gaming, and other creative projects. It is important to note that the generated images should be reviewed and used with care, as they may not be entirely original and could be influenced by the training data.

3. Lumen5

Lumen5 is a content creation platform that uses AI to help users create videos, social media posts, and other types of content. It has several features that make it useful for content creation and marketing, including:

Pros:

  • Automatically summarizes text from a blog post, article, or another source into a script for a video or social media post
  • Offers a library of royalty-free videos, images, and music to use in content
  • Has a drag-and-drop interface for easy content creation
  • Can create videos in multiple languages
  • Has a built-in analytics tool to track the performance of created content.

Cons:

  • The quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material
  • The automatic summarization feature may not always capture the main points of the source material
  • The library of videos, images, and music is limited.
  • The analytics feature is basic

Overall, Lumen5 is a useful tool for creating content quickly and easily, it can help automate the process of creating videos, social media posts, and other types of content. However, the quality of the generated content may vary depending on the source material and it is important to review and edit the content before publishing it.

4. Grammarly

Grammarly is a writing-enhancement platform that uses AI to check for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text. It also provides suggestions for improving the clarity, concision, and readability of the text. It has several features that make it useful for improving writing, including:

Pros:

  • Checks for grammar, punctuation, and spelling errors in the text
  • Provides suggestions for improving clarity, concision, and readability
  • Can be integrated with various apps and platforms such as Microsoft Office, Google Docs, and social media platforms
  • Offers a browser extension and a desktop app
  • Has a premium version with more advanced features such as plagiarism detection and more

Cons:

  • The suggestions provided may not always be accurate or appropriate
  • The grammar checker may not always recognize context-specific language use
  • The free version has limited features
  • Limited to English language only
  • Overall, Grammarly is a useful tool for improving writing, it can help users identify and correct grammar and punctuation errors, and improve the clarity, concision, and readability of their text. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate.

5.OpenAI Codex

OpenAI Codex is a system developed by OpenAI that can create code from natural language descriptions of software tasks. The system is based on the GPT-3 model and can generate code in multiple programming languages.

Pros:

  • Can automate the process of writing code
  • Can help developers to be more productive
  • Can help non-technical people to create software
  • Can generate code in multiple programming languages

Cons:

  • The quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description
  • The generated code may not always be optimal or efficient
  • The system may not be able to handle complex software tasks
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code.

Overall, OpenAI Codex is a powerful tool that can help automate the process of writing code and make it more accessible to non-technical people. However, the quality of the generated code may vary depending on the task description and it is important to review and test the code before using it in a production environment. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

6. Tabnine

Tabnine is a code completion tool that uses AI to predict and suggest code snippets. It is compatible with multiple programming languages and can be integrated with various code editors.

Pros:

  • Can improve coding efficiency by suggesting code snippets based on context
  • Can complete entire code blocks
  • Can predict variables, functions, and other elements of code
  • Can be integrated with various code editors

Cons:

  • The suggestions may not always be accurate or appropriate
  • The system may not always be able to understand the context of the code
  • May not work with all code editors
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the code.

Overall, TabNine is a useful tool for developers that can help improve coding efficiency and reduce the time spent on writing code. However, it is important to review the suggestions provided by the tool and use them with caution, as they may not always be accurate or appropriate. It is important to use the tool as an aid, not a replacement for the developer's knowledge.

7. Jasper AI

Jasper is a content writing and content generation tool that uses artificial intelligence to identify the best words and sentences for your writing style and medium in the most efficient, quick, and accessible way.

Pros:

  • User-friendly interface
  • Generates a wide variety of content types
  • Guarantees 100% unique and free-plagiarism content
  • SEO friendly
  •  Create articles of up to 10k words

Cons:

8. Surfer SEO

Surfer SEO is a software tool designed to help website owners and digital marketers improve their search engine optimization (SEO) efforts. The tool provides a variety of features that can be used to analyze a website's on-page SEO, including:

Features:

  • A site audit tool that checks for technical SEO issues
  • A content editor that suggests optimizations for individual pages
  • A keyword research tool that suggests keywords to target
  • A SERP analyzer that shows how a website's pages rank for specific keywords
  • A backlink analysis tool that shows the backlinks pointing to a website.

Pros:

  • Can help website owners and marketers identify technical SEO issues
  • Can provide suggestions for optimizing individual pages
  • Can help with keyword research
  • Can show how a website's pages rank for specific keywords
  • Can provide insight into a website's backlink profile

Cons:

  • Some features may require a paid subscription
  • The tool is not a guarantee of better ranking
  • The tool can only analyze the data it has access to
  • The tool's suggestions may not always be applicable or optimal

Overall, Surfer SEO can be a useful tool for website owners and digital marketers looking to improve their SEO efforts. However, it is important to remember that it is just a tool and should be used in conjunction with other SEO best practices. Additionally, the tool is not a guarantee of better ranking.

9. Zapier

Zapier is a web automation tool that allows users to automate repetitive tasks by connecting different web applications together. It does this by creating "Zaps" that automatically move data between apps, and can also be used to trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app.

Features:

  • Can connect over 3,000 web applications
  • Can automate repetitive tasks
  • Can create "Zaps" to move data between apps
  • Can trigger certain actions in one app based on events in another app.

Pros:

  • Can automate repetitive tasks
  • Can save time
  • Can improve workflow
  • Can increase productivity
  • Can be integrated with a wide range of web applications

Cons:

  • Can be difficult to set up
  • May require some technical skills
  • May require a paid subscription for some features
  • Some apps may not be compatible
  • Dependence on the tool may lead to a lack of understanding of the apps

Overall, Zapier is a useful tool that can help users automate repetitive tasks and improve workflow. It can save time and increase productivity by connecting different web applications together. #9760. The Hardest McDonald's Item To Prepare, According To One Former Worker

There are quite a few challenges, actually, when it comes to working at McDonald's. There's a lot of time management involved, as well as customer service and interaction, to say nothing of the physical fatigue from being on your feet for hours. Then there's the actual assembly of the food itself, and while the burger chain with nearly 42,000 locations across the globe has automated many facets of its kitchen, for the most part, employees must still work the machines and put the sandwiches together. So all this begs the question: Is there a menu item that is the hardest to prepare? Food Republic spoke with Tristen Epps-Long, who won Season 22 of "Top Chef" and who is actually a former McDonald's chef, and in his opinion, the dubious honor belongs to the Big Mac.

His reasoning? "It's multi-layered," he said. And there's the fact that there isn't a mold; it's all hand-stacked, with many different parts, including three buns, two burger patties, a slice of cheese, pickles, onion, and lettuce. "It was just a bit more hand work," Epps-Long told us. It seems other McDonald's employees agree with our expert, too, as one person on Reddit reported they had a coworker almost quit after receiving an order for 12 Big Macs at once. It is worth noting, though, that Epps-Long did mention that, after a while, Big Macs can lose their undesirable status; you just have to get the hang of making them.

Peruse any discussion board where McDonald's employees are chatting about what their least favorite menu item is to make, and aside from Big Macs (which get plenty of mentions), the Quarter Pounder (and its variants) comes up quite frequently. It's understandable; the QP is the only McDonald's burger that's cooked fresh, not frozen, so there would be an extra layer of food safety that employees would have to follow in order to prevent cross-contamination with the raw beef product.

On the dessert side, the apple pies seem to be a pain to make as well, as one employee on Reddit recounted how the sweet treats take six minutes in the deep fryer, which is apparently long enough to start doing other tasks, but not long enough to finish the tasks before the pies are done. That individual must work at an overseas location as apple pies are baked in the USA. The McFlurries appear to be another annoying menu item to make, likely because the process is so hands-on; unlike the burgers, which get cooked on a timed clam shell grill, employees have to hold the McFlurry cup during every step.

Now, at the other end of the spectrum, Tristen Epps-Long shared that he found the Egg McMuffin to be one of the easiest things to make, which is slightly surprising, as there are quite a few different elements to it. However, on Reddit, a commenter remarked that the easiest thing for them to make is the plain burgers or cheeseburgers, and this apparently resonated with their peers because the statement has 43 upvotes.

#9757. Not Ribeye: Bobby Flay Recommends This Steak Cut For The Best Tacos

When taco night rolls around, you'll want to head to the butcher and grab some good meat. If you're making carne asada, your instinct might be to pick the ribeye. While it might be the gold standard of steak, tacos and ribeye are an inherent mismatch. Tacos are one of the most democratic foods out there, while ribeye is made for deep pockets and expensive tastes. Even Food Network's Bobby Flay recommends skipping it. Instead, he swaps the pricey cut for the seriously underrated skirt steak.

Ribeye is America's favorite steak thanks to its rich marbling and tender texture, but you'll rarely find it in taquerias. Beyond being pricey, ribeye's assets are its downfall in tacos. In an interview with Food and Wine, Flay revealed the reason why he often chooses to skip ribeye altogether: "[Ribeye] can be inconsistent because the fat doesn't always melt even when cooked properly." This is a real problem in tacos. Encased in a taco, you don't have the option to trim around a rubbery pocket of fat or leave it on the plate. Even if you trim the fat before adding the steak to your tacos, it's so unevenly distributed that you risk ending up with wildly inconsistent slices.

Unlike ribeye, skirt is cut from the plate primal, a hard-working area near the diaphragm. Rather than being streaked with generous ribbons of fat, it's comprised of long, coarse muscle fibers, which give it a chewier, more fibrous bite along with a bold, beef-forward flavor. Its thin profile may not win it fans at white tablecloth restaurants, but it's exactly why taquerias can't get enough of it. All that surface area compared to its thickness means skirt steak cooks quickly, soaks up marinades fast, and slices evenly, which is everything you want from taco meat.

There's no cut of beef more well-suited to carne asada than skirt. Literally translating to "grilled meat," the beef is usually marinated in a citrus and garlic blend, with the acidic ingredients helping to tenderize the surface of the meat. After being left to soak up the flavor for a couple of hours, it's then seared or grilled over an open flame or charcoal to impart a smoky, charred flavor (an air fryer also works if you can't grill). Because skirt is such a thin cut, it doesn't enjoy spending too much time over high heat; it only needs around two to four minutes per side. Skirt can be prone to drying out, so it would be wise to avoid cooking past a medium doneness.

How you cut skirt is just as important as how you cook it. Compared to other cuts, skirt has particularly long, dense muscle fibers, and if you slice them with the grain, you'll leave them intact, resulting in chewy, rubbery bites. Slicing against the grain shortens these fibers, turning them into more satisfying, bite-sized strands. To identify the grain, look closely at the surface of the meat to spot the direction of the muscle fibers running through the beef.

Although skirt is beloved by taquerias, that doesn't make it suited to all beef tacos. One popular style where we would skip skirt is birria, the slow-cooked, tender beef marinated in a chili-and-spice adobo served with a flavorful broth for dipping. The whole concept of birria revolves around slow-braising, requiring tough, collagen-rich cuts like chuck or beef cheek, which break down into tender, shreddable meat over several hours. While skirt does have some connective tissue, it's simply too thin and lean to survive hours of prolonged heat.

#9755. This Vitamin Reduces Depression Symptoms By 50%

One vitamin reduced depression symptoms after a month, but the benefit depended on how participants felt at the start.

One vitamin reduced depression symptoms after a month, but the benefit depended on how participants felt at the start.

Taking a high dose of vitamin B6 for a month reduced depression symptoms in people already experiencing them.

The vitamin helps the brain produce chemical messengers involved in mood regulation.

The findings suggest a potential role for B6 in treating depression, although larger clinical trials are needed.

Almost 270 adults, mostly young women, took part in the research.

They were randomly assigned to take either 100 mg of vitamin B6, vitamin B12 or a placebo each day for around a month.

Among almost 60 people with at least mild depression symptoms at the start, those taking B6 improved more than those receiving B12 or a placebo.

Average depression scores fell by about 54 percent in the symptomatic B6 group, compared with 24 percent in the placebo group.

The benefit remained after accounting for differences in how severe their symptoms had been at the start.

The findings come from a new analysis of data collected in the same research programme that previously reported reduced anxiety after B6 supplementation.

Vitamin B6 supports several processes involved in regulating mood.

Dr David Field, the study’s first author, said:

“Vitamin B6 plays a crucial role in the production of several chemical messengers in the brain, including serotonin and GABA, both of which are central to mood regulation.”

GABA helps restrain nerve cell activity, contributing to the balance between excitation and inhibition in the brain.

Increasing B6 availability could boost their production, potentially explaining the improvement in depression symptoms.

Inflammation may also play a role, potentially affecting both depression and how the body uses B6.

Vitamin B6 occurs naturally in foods including poultry, fish, chickpeas, bananas and fortified cereals.

However, the trial tested a high supplement dose, rather than a change in everyday food intake.

High doses of B6 can cause peripheral nerve damage, so the researchers say supplementation at these doses requires medical supervision.

Larger trials now need to establish the most effective dose, monitor safety and determine whether B6 could help alongside existing depression treatments.

The study was published in the journal Depression and Anxiety (Field et al., 2026).

#9753. Add This Creamy Dip To Ground Beef For Juicier, More Flavorful Burgers

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

The perfect burger can be hard to come by. When you're going out, Food Republic's list of the best burgers in every state can be helpful, and there are even some great fast food options. But when you're looking for a super juicy and flavorful homemade grilled or pan-fried patty, what's the best route to take?

Sometimes, it all comes down to what you mix into the ground beef. While Bobby Flay uses only salt and pepper to season his patties, some folks swear by Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder for a kick of flavor. But there's one ingredient you may not have thought of that will keep your end result wonderfully succulent. Try mixing some onion dip into your ground beef. It's one of the clever ingredients that make burgers juicier, and it will add loads of flavor.

Onion dips generally come seasoned with dried onion and garlic, salt, and other herbs, plus a little sugar for sweetness. Add to that the sour cream base, and you have a rich, bold, slightly tangy, umami-filled burst of flavor that won't overpower your taste buds. And because you're mixing the dip directly into the beef before cooking, it can help keep your patties nice and moist (as long as you don't overcook them). Sour cream is simply cultured cream, so it has a high moisture content, and the added seasonings aren't so coarse that they will burn before the beef itself is cooked.

When it comes to what dip to use, classics like Dean's French Onion or Daisy Sour Cream French Onion, which is available on Amazon, will work great, but pretty much any brand will work. Depending on how much tangy flavor you want, you'll need about a half-cup to a full cup of dip per 2 pounds of beef.

The beauty of using onion dip in your burgers is that it's a one-ingredient solution, but you can increase the intensity with extra onion powder or fresh minced or dried onions. Just don't overdo it on the onion pieces, or the patties could fall apart on the grill. If you're going heavy on the amount of dip you use, you may want to think about adding some breadcrumbs as a binding agent. Dried parsley makes a great mix-in, as do other Italian herbs, but you should start sparingly so they don't overpower the flavor you're aiming for.

As for toppings, the regular stuff will do, but you might want to hold off on the ketchup and mustard until you've had a bite. Caramelized onions are an obvious choice, or you can give your burger some crunch with crispy fried onions. And you can always add an extra dollop of onion dip on top for more creamy flavor and texture.

Lastly, this trick will also work with a dried dip mix. Just mix it in with sour cream before you make the burgers. And if you want a similarly juicy bite without the added zing, try using mayonnaise in your burger. But for a juicy texture and plenty of zesty flavor, grab that onion dip out of the fridge.
